en: n. a state in which people do not know what to do or what is happening; a situation in which you cannot tell one thing from another; a mistake in which one thing is thought to be another
ex: There was a lot of confusion at the airport after the flight was canceled.
班機取消後，機場一片混亂。

en: a. not complete or whole; showing unfair support for one person or side; having a special liking for something; n. a section of a musical note
ex: He made a partial payment and promised to pay the rest next month.
他先付了一部分款項，並承諾下個月付清其餘。

en: n. an act of breaking a law, rule or agreement; the act of disturbing something that should be respected; the act of treating something with no respect
ex: Parking here is a violation of city regulations.
在這裡停車違反了市府規定。

en: a. done according to a fixed plan or system; thorough and organized; relating to a classification system
ex: The police conducted a systematic search of the area.
警方對該地區進行了有系統的搜索。

en: n. a physical or mental condition that makes it difficult for someone to do certain things; the state of being unable to do something; a legal condition that stops someone from doing something
ex: The school offers special programs for students with disabilities.
學校為身心障礙的學生提供特別課程。

en: n. one of the sharp curved nails on the feet of birds and some animals; the part of the body of a crab or lobster used for holding; v. to scratch or tear something with claws; to climb or move with difficulty
ex: The cat sharpened its claws on the sofa.
那隻貓在沙發上磨爪子。

en: a. small in size, amount or degree; thin and not strong; n. an act or remark that shows that you do not respect someone; vt. to treat someone with a lack of respect
ex: There was a slight change in the weather this morning.
今天早上天氣有一點輕微變化。

en: n. a unit of energy, used to measure the amount of energy that food provides; a unit of heat
ex: A slice of pizza contains about three hundred calories.
一片披薩大約含有三百卡路里。

en: vt. to change words from one language into another; to change something into a different form; to explain the meaning of something; vi. to be changed into another language; to have a particular meaning in practice
ex: Can you translate this sentence into English for me?
你能幫我把這個句子翻成英文嗎？

en: n. a common drug used to reduce pain, fever and inflammation; a tablet of this drug
ex: She took an aspirin to ease her headache.
她吃了一顆阿斯匹靈來緩解頭痛。

en: n. the natural features of a place, such as mountains, trees and rivers; the painted background on a theater stage
ex: We took photos of the beautiful mountain scenery.
我們拍了美麗山景的照片。

en: n. a lack of knowledge or information about something; the state of not knowing about something
ex: Ignorance of the law is no excuse.
不知法律不能作為藉口。

en: n. a person whose job is to check, repair or use technical equipment; a person who is skilled at a practical or technical job
ex: A technician came to fix our broken air conditioner.
一位技師來修我們壞掉的冷氣機。

en: n. a person who is admired or loved very much; a statue or image that is worshipped; a popular star such as a singer or actor; a false idea or belief
ex: She is a pop idol with millions of fans.
她是擁有數百萬粉絲的流行偶像。

en: a. feeling or showing that you have no hope; (of a situation) very bad or serious; willing to do anything to get what you want because you are in a very bad situation
ex: The villagers were desperate for clean water.
村民迫切需要乾淨的水。

en: n. a person who enters a building illegally in order to steal things
ex: A burglar broke into the shop through the back window.
一名竊賊從後窗闖入店裡。

en: n. a careful study of a subject in order to discover new facts; the activity of finding information; vi. to study something in detail to discover facts; vt. to study a subject in detail
ex: She is doing research on how plants grow in dry soil.
她正在研究植物如何在乾燥土壤中生長。

en: n. a diagram showing the relationship between two sets of numbers; a drawing that shows how something changes; vt. to show something on a graph
ex: The graph shows how sales have increased over the past year.
這張圖表顯示了去年銷售額如何增加。

en: a. clearly seen or understood; easy to notice; obvious
ex: It was evident that he had been crying.
他顯然哭過。

en: n. the process of getting used to a new situation or place; training for new members of an organization; the direction something faces; a person's attitude or beliefs
ex: New students attended an orientation session before classes began.
新生在開學前參加了新生說明會。

en: n. the management of large amounts of money by governments or companies; the money available to a person or organization; vt. to provide money for something; vi. to raise money
ex: He works in finance at a large bank.
他在一家大銀行從事金融工作。

en: a. impossible or very hard to believe; extremely good, great or large
ex: The view from the mountain top was incredible.
山頂的景色美得令人難以置信。

en: a. showing care and effort in your work or duties; hardworking and careful
ex: She is a diligent student who always finishes her homework.
她是個勤奮的學生，總是完成作業。

en: n. the empty space at the side of a printed page; the edge or border of something; the amount by which one thing is greater than another; an amount of space or time that is allowed for something
ex: She wrote her comments in the margin of the book.
她把評語寫在書的頁邊空白處。

en: n. a long journey, especially by sea or in space; vi. to make a long journey; vt. to travel over or across something
ex: The voyage from England to America took six weeks.
從英國到美國的航程花了六週。

en: a. relating to the body rather than the mind; real and able to be touched or seen; relating to the laws of physics; n. a medical examination to check your health
ex: Regular physical exercise is important for good health.
規律的體能運動對健康很重要。

en: a. useful and helpful rather than negative; relating to building or making something
ex: She gave me some constructive criticism on my essay.
她對我的文章提出了一些建設性的批評。

en: n. an insect or small animal that damages crops or food; a person or thing that is very annoying; (old use) a deadly disease
ex: Mice and rats are common household pests.
老鼠是常見的居家害蟲。

en: a. relating to literature; connected with writing or books; knowing a lot about books and writing
ex: He won a literary prize for his first novel.
他以第一本小說贏得了文學獎。

en: a. involving a complete or very great change in something; relating to a political revolution; n. a person who supports or takes part in a revolution
ex: The invention of the internet was truly revolutionary.
網際網路的發明真的具有革命性。

en: n. a government department that is responsible for a particular area; the work or position of a priest or minister; a group of ministers who form a government
ex: She works at the Ministry of Education.
她在教育部工作。

en: n. a border or support that surrounds a picture, door or window; the basic structure of something; the build of a person's body; vt. to put something in a frame; to express something in a particular way; to make someone appear guilty by false evidence
ex: She put the photo in a silver frame.
她把照片放進銀色相框裡。

en: n. a way of thinking that is clear and sensible; the science of correct reasoning; the principles used in the design of a computer system
ex: There is no logic in what he said.
他說的話毫無邏輯。

en: n. a thin white layer of ice that forms on surfaces when the temperature is very low; very cold weather; an unfriendly feeling; vt. to cover something with frost; vi. to become covered with frost
ex: There was heavy frost on the grass this morning.
今天早上草地上結了厚厚的霜。

en: n. one of the foods or substances that are combined to make a particular dish or product; a part of something
ex: Flour and sugar are the main ingredients of this cake.
麵粉和糖是這個蛋糕的主要成分。

en: n. harm done to someone as a punishment for what they did to you; the desire to hurt someone who has hurt you; vt. to harm someone in return for harm done to you
ex: He wanted revenge for the way they had treated him.
他想報復他們對待他的方式。

en: vt. to process used materials so that they can be used again; to use something again; n. a process of recycling materials
ex: We recycle all our glass and plastic bottles.
我們回收所有玻璃瓶和塑膠瓶。

en: vt. to give someone the desire and confidence to do something; to fill someone with a feeling; to cause someone to have a new idea; vi. to breathe air into your lungs
ex: Her story inspired many young people to study science.
她的故事激勵了許多年輕人去學科學。

en: vt. to make someone feel shy, ashamed or uncomfortable in front of other people; to cause someone to feel awkward; to cause financial or other difficulties
ex: He was embarrassed when he forgot her name.
他忘了她的名字，覺得很尷尬。

en: a. relating to technology or the use of technology; connected with machines, tools or processes
ex: Technological advances have changed the way we communicate.
科技的進步改變了我們的溝通方式。
